_doc: Upstream gauge registry: which gauges feed each target station, and how.
Keys are OpenFlow site ids (same format as .github/site_ids.txt).
site_id     -- daily history source for TRAINING (DWR:<abbrev> or USGS:<id>)
usgs_id     -- USGS id used to delineate the gauged area (NLDI) when building basin_zones.json
nws_lid     -- NWS gauge id; NWPS supplies ~30 days of observations and the current RFC forecast (inference + routing CLI)
lag_days    -- daily travel time used for the ML 'upstream_flow' feature: upstream_flow(d) = sum_i weight_i * Q_i(d - lag_days_i)
weight      -- relative contribution in that routed sum (absorbs reach gains / diversion losses)
lag_hours / k_hours -- hourly routing defaults (pure travel time + linear-reservoir attenuation) used by routing.py when
the recent calibration window is too quiet to fit them; normally they are re-fit on the last ~4 weeks.
forecast_days -- how many days of RFC forecast to expect at the upstream gauges (ML decoder 'upstream_known' horizon = min(lag_days) + forecast_days)
Defaults for USGS:08276500 were calibrated on the Oct 23-31 2026 flood (Rio Grande at Alamosa + Conejos nr Mogote -> Taos Junction Bridge, RMSE ~150 cfs).
Stations with an empty `upstream` list are forecast from the NWS RFC forecast for the gauge itself (mode `nws`) when one is current.
